sections.h2: Where do I take a Cumberland County deed for recording?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds works out of the Historic Courthouse at One Courthouse Square in Carlisle. Every deed, mortgage and related paper for land in the county's boroughs and townships lands in its index.

The counter opens on weekdays, with an occasional remote day, and closes at four in the afternoon. Because of that, the office wants visitors to book an appointment first. Notaries and anyone filing a subdivision plan must have one. Call 717.240.6370 or email recorder@cumberlandcountypa.gov to set a time.

Most sellers never go. The closing agent drafts the deed, collects the money and sends the package in on the seller's behalf.

sections.h2: What is the price of recording a deed in Cumberland?
sections.html:
Recording a deed runs $104.75 on the price list dated November 17, 2025. That figure folds in the $20 parcel identifier charge where one is needed, and every parcel beyond the first adds another $20.

Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds price list dated November 17, 2025
DocumentFee
Deed$104.75
Mortgage$104.75
Satisfaction piece$78.25
Assignment of mortgage$78.25
Agreement of sale$78.25
Power of attorney with a parcel number$37.00
Notary public$34.00
Subdivision plan$47.00

Source: the Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds fee schedule. Past the fourth page, each sheet adds $2.00, and a name beyond the fourth adds fifty cents. A Statement of Value costs $1.00 more.

A one dollar increase in the Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025 is why deed and mortgage prices rose on that date. Per the county FAQ, Harrisburg sets most amounts, while the parcel identifier fee comes from a county ordinance.

sections.h2: How is realty transfer tax collected on a Cumberland County sale?
sections.html:
The Recorder takes the tax at the counter when a taxable deed arrives. The county's FAQ describes the full burden as 2% of the price: one point to the Commonwealth, and the other point shared equally by the municipality and the school district. Money moves to those bodies at month end, and the county keeps 1% of the state's portion and 2% of the local portion as a commission.

  • Under state law the grantor and grantee answer jointly for the tax, which makes the sale contract the place to assign it.
  • Some family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy are exempt. Staff do not rule on exemptions, so ask a lawyer or the Revenue Department.
  • The Statement of Value, form REV-183, goes with the deed when an exemption is claimed, when the real consideration differs from the figure on the deed's face, or when the deed is over 30 days old.

A $310,000 house sale produces $6,200 in combined transfer tax before recording fees.

sections.h2: Does Cumberland County take electronic recordings?
sections.html:
Yes, through three vendors only: ePN, CSC and Simplifile. The county says attorneys and title companies file most documents this way.

Paper still works. A mailed deed needs original signatures and notary stamps, since a photocopy cannot be recorded. If the check or card amount is wrong, the package comes back unfiled, unless the overage is $10 or less, in which case the office keeps the difference and records the paper.

Write checks to Recorder of Deeds. Cards go through Value Payment Systems with a 2.25% charge, a $2.50 floor, and 3% on business cards. Cash refunds are not given.

sections.h2: How old are the deed books held in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
The office has kept a continuous record since 1750, so a title search can reach deeds from the colonial period. Its history page says the books came through the courthouse fire of 1845 unscathed and were hidden away during the Confederate invasion of 1863.

Until 1929 every instrument was copied by hand into canvas bound volumes. Typed books followed, with separate indexes for deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers until December 1993, when the index was computerized. Paper books ended in 2001, and the old volumes moved from the courthouse to the County Archives in November 2017.

Landex lets anyone search back to 1750 around the clock, and the office has public computers for the same job. Searches run by name rather than address. To learn who owns a given parcel, ask the Tax Assessment Office or use the county's GIS Property Mapper.

sections.h2: What should a Cumberland County seller check around recording?
sections.html:
Clear every lien before closing, because the Recorder only holds mortgages and secured transactions. The county FAQ says judgment liens, municipal liens and state tax liens are filed with the Prothonotary, so a title search should cover both offices.

  • A lender records a satisfaction piece when a mortgage is paid. The homeowner receives no new deed.
  • Staff are neither bonded nor allowed to search title or advise on law. Hire a title searcher, an abstract company or an attorney.
  • Plans from the early 1900s onward may be on file, and the deed's property description often cites a plan book and page.
  • A veteran can record a DD214, and a certified copy is free should the original be lost. Discharge papers stay closed to public view.

For properties that reach the Tax Claim Bureau's online upset sale, the 2026 sale terms add transfer tax and recording fees on top of the winning bid. The tax is the assessed value, times the Common Level Ratio Factor, times 2%.

The county's upset sale Q&A says there is no redemption period once a sale closes. An owner may still file objections or exceptions with the local court up to thirty days after the court's confirmation nisi of the consolidated return. The 2026 continued sale was held online through Bid4Assets on October 23, and an owner with back tax should call the Tax Claim Bureau at 717-240-6367 before any listing goes live.

sections.h2: What is the Cumberland County housing picture for a seller?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures for the county show 277,270 people in the July 2025 estimate, 6.9% more than the 2020 base, living on 545.48 square miles. In 2020 that worked out to 475.7 people for each square mile.

QuickFacts counts 114,465 housing units. Owners live in 71.3% of occupied homes, and the middle owner occupied value is $277,600 for 2020 to 2024. A typical household brings in $87,494, and typical gross rent is $1,249. Permits for 745 buildings were issued in 2025.

The 2026 county rate is 2.875 mills, with municipal and school rates added. Totals on the county's sheet run from about 15.95 mills in Hampden Township to about 27.27 mills in Newville Borough, so where the house sits matters a lot for the annual bill.

faqs.q: What does Cumberland charge for a deed recording?
faqs.a: The charge is $104.75 on the price list dated November 17, 2025, with the $20 parcel identifier fee included where required. Pages past four are $2.00 each and names past four are fifty cents each. Transfer tax is paid on top.

faqs.q: Which party owes the transfer tax on a Cumberland County sale?
faqs.a: Both do, as far as the state is concerned: grantor and grantee answer jointly. Who actually pays is a matter for the sale contract. The tax totals 2% and is collected when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder of Deeds research my title?
faqs.a: No. The staff may not conduct title searches or give legal advice, though they can show you how to use the public terminals. Records are indexed by name, so a searcher looks up owners rather than addresses.

faqs.q: Does paying off a mortgage produce a new deed?
faqs.a: No. The lender files a satisfaction piece to show the loan is paid, and the original deed remains your proof of ownership. A copy of the deed can be bought through Landex or requested by email from the office.

faqs.q: Can documents be filed by mail or electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, with conditions. A mailed package needs original signatures, notary stamps and the exact fee. Electronic filing must come through ePN, CSC or Simplifile. Plans and notary filings need an appointment.
